title: The Frank!Framework moves 10,000+ production integrations but records nothing about what each exchange decided
content:
The Frank!Framework is Apache-2.0 licensed and, per the research, already runs more than 10,000 integrations in production. Its function is to move messages between systems. What it does not do is keep a business record of what each exchange decided, which is a different concern from whether the message was delivered successfully.

That is the gap in its strongest available form: the framework's own purpose excludes the record layer, so the missing piece is complementary rather than competitive. The research puts the seam at one adapter — the framework's existing extension mechanism — which bounds the integration cost and makes it legible to the people who maintain the code.

Licence and installed base are what make this the strongest fit in this part of the corpus. Apache-2.0 means a contribution can be taken upstream without a licensing negotiation, and the existing deployments mean the record layer arrives wherever the framework already runs, so the value does not depend on winning clients one at a time.
